Trucking Accidents

What to Do After a Trucking Accident on the Florida Panhandle

Truck crash evidence has a short shelf life. What you do in the first week can determine what is provable.

Published May 19, 2026 · The Price Law Firm

A crash with a commercial truck is not simply a worse car accident. The injuries tend to be more severe, the opposition is better resourced, and critically, the most valuable evidence can be gone within days.

The first week matters more than in an ordinary crash

Major carriers often dispatch a rapid response team to the scene within hours — investigators and sometimes counsel, documenting the crash while it is fresh and while you are still in a hospital bed. They are building the carrier's defense from day one.

Meanwhile the electronic evidence is on a timer. Engine control module data, electronic logging device records, dashcam footage and internal dispatch communications are frequently overwritten or purged on routine retention schedules. Once gone, they generally cannot be recovered.

What a preservation letter does

One of the first steps an attorney takes is sending a spoliation letter — formal notice demanding the carrier preserve all relevant evidence: black box and ECM data, driver logs and hours-of-service records, the driver qualification file, maintenance and inspection history, cargo loading documentation, dashcam footage, dispatch communications, and drug and alcohol testing records.

Sent early, it locks the record in place. Sent late, it arrives after the data has cycled.

At the scene, if you are able

  • Get medical attention immediately — truck crash injuries are frequently more serious than they first appear.
  • Photograph the truck's markings: company name, USDOT number, trailer number and license plates. These identify the carrier.
  • Photograph both vehicles, their resting positions, debris, skid marks and road conditions.
  • Collect witness names and phone numbers.
  • Do not give a recorded statement to the carrier's insurer or investigator.

Why there is usually more than one defendant

Responsibility in a truck crash may be shared among the driver, the motor carrier, a broker or shipper, the company that loaded the trailer, the owner of the tractor or trailer, a maintenance contractor, or a parts manufacturer. Each typically carries separate insurance — which matters enormously when injuries are severe and a single policy would never be enough.

The Panhandle corridor

I-10 through Jackson County carries constant long-haul freight, and US-231 and Highway 98 move heavy commercial traffic through Bay County. If a truck has injured you on any of them, call 850-215-2195 as soon as you can. The sooner preservation letters go out, the more of the record survives.
